# subject: ENG-205
# topic: Sixteenth Century Reading Quiz
# title: ENG-205 16th Century (1485-1603) — 2 Q&A (quiz-style)
# short: 2 Q&A (quiz-style)
In what year was Henry VII crowned, starting the Tudor dynasty and the sixteenth-century literary period?
Which two royal houses fought the Wars of the Roses, and what were their emblems?
column2: York, whose emblem was the white rose, and Lancaster, whose emblem was the red rose.

column1: At what battle did Yorkist King Richard III die, ending the Wars of the Roses?
column2: The battle of Bosworth Field.

column1: How did Henry VII unite the rival houses of York and Lancaster?
column2: He married Elizabeth of York.

column1: How much did London grow between 1520 and 1650?
column2: It grew from 60,000 people to 375,000, making it Europe's fastest-growing city.

column1: What does the word "Renaissance" literally mean?
column2: Rebirth.

column1: Which humanist changed outmoded school curricula to prepare young men for public service?
column2: Erasmus.

column1: What subjects made up the medieval trivium?
column2: Grammar, logic, and rhetoric.

column1: What subjects made up the medieval quadrivium?
column2: Arithmetic, geometry, astronomy, and music.

column1: What were young aristocratic women taught?
column2: Modern languages, religion, music, and needlework, and increasingly to read, though not necessarily to write.

column1: When and where did Martin Luther begin the Reformation?
column2: In Germany in November 1517, when he posted his Ninety-Five Theses protesting Catholic corruption.

column1: What principally motivated England's Reformation, according to the notes?
column2: King Henry VIII's greed and his succession troubles, since Catherine of Aragon had not given him a legitimate son.

column1: What did the Act of Supremacy declare?
column2: That King Henry VIII was Supreme Head of the Church of England.

column1: What did Henry VIII do between 1536 and 1539?
column2: He seized the lands and wealth of England's Catholic religious houses and gave them to his followers.

column1: Who wrote the Book of Common Prayer and the 42 articles of religion, and under which king?
column2: Archbishop of Canterbury Thomas Cranmer, during the reign of Edward VI.

column1: Why was Mary I called "Bloody" Mary?
column2: Because she persecuted Protestants while restoring Roman Catholicism from 1553 to 1558.

column1: Who were Recusants, and how did Elizabeth treat them?
column2: People who did not attend Anglican services, and Elizabeth fined them.

column1: Which mythological and biblical figures did poets and painters compare Elizabeth to?
column2: The goddesses Diana, Astraea, and Cynthia, and the biblical heroine Deborah.

column1: Who was Elizabeth's spymaster?
column2: Walsingham, who helped her run a massive spy network.

column1: Who sent the Spanish Armada against England, and why?
column2: King Philip II of Spain, to reclaim England for the Catholic Church after Elizabeth beheaded Mary Queen of Scots.

column1: Which king expelled the Jews from England, and when?
column2: King Edward I, in 1290.

column1: What guild owned all printing presses?
column2: The Stationers' Company.

column1: What is the most important piece of literary criticism of the sixteenth century?
column2: Philip Sidney's Defense of Poesy.

column1: What seven literary modes does Sidney's Defense of Poesy name?
column2: Pastoral, heroic, lyric, satiric, elegiac, tragic, and comic.

column1: Whose adoption of blank verse revolutionized theatrical expression?
column2: Christopher Marlowe's.

column1: Who played female roles on the Elizabethan stage?
column2: Boy actors, since no women appeared on stage.

column1: Which group especially opposed the theater, and why?
column2: Puritans, who charged that boys dressed as women would excite illicit sexual desire.

column1: Who succeeded Elizabeth I in 1603?
column2: James VI of Scotland, son of Mary Queen of Scots, who ruled England as James I.
